visualBrief: Two rust-brown steel ribs support the straight deck through slender spandrel columns. Cross-braced steelwork, concrete footings, a lower maintenance walk, four traffic lanes, sidewalks and simple lamps follow exterior photos.
observations: Twin rust-brown steel arch ribs carry the high road deck through vertical spandrel posts. Diagonals and transverse bracing span between the ribs.
The open lower steelwork includes maintenance walkways. The underside of the pale deck is ribbed and the two road edges carry narrow sidewalks, vertical rail bars and simple lamps.
limitations: The steel span uses the straight plan and published dimensions from the municipal repair inventory. Satellite views differ over the elevated deck; the bridge axis ties to the mapped road ends.
The two mapped bridge traces determine the replacement masks. The modeled sidewalks follow the deck edges and transition to the mapped footway at the island landing.
Deck elevations, the arch profile and the local approach grading are exterior visual estimates. The west approach compensates for the steep drop in the standard terrain samples.
